parsed.headline: Former President Barack Obama campaigns for Democrats while criticizing the Trump administration

pages.text: Former President Barack Obama criticized the Trump administration regarding the war in Iran and high consumer prices during campaign events for Democrats ahead of the U.S. midterm elections. Speaking to crowds in Ohio and Michigan on October 24, 2026, Obama targeted President Donald Trump and his cabinet members, including mocking the president's efforts to redecorate the White House. In Cleveland, Obama stated that after two years of what he described as chaos, cruelty, corruption, and incompetence, voters have a chance to say, 'enough is enough.' He characterized the upcoming election as the last best chance to rein in the administration's 'foolishness.' While acknowledging that voters rejected Democrats in 2024 due to economic and inflation concerns following the Covid pandemic, Obama asserted that the president is responsible for the current state of the economy, noting that prices are more expensive now than they were previously.

During a rally in Georgia, President Trump touted his administration's tariff and immigration policies, telling supporters the country is in a 'golden age of America.' Addressing economic concerns, Trump acknowledged that oil prices are 'temporarily high' but stated that pump prices will decrease as the country grows stronger. The president has faced pressure to lower fuel prices, which have risen due to wars in Iran and Ukraine. On October 24, 2026, Trump cast his ballot in Florida alongside First Lady Melania Trump as early voting has begun. The midterm elections, scheduled for November 3, will determine which party controls Congress for the remainder of the president's term.

parsed.headline: Saint Martin’s Island in Bangladesh scheduled to reopen to tourists on 1 November

pages.text: Saint Martin’s Island is set to reopen to visitors on 1 November following a closure lasting nearly 10 months. According to Prothom Alo English, tourist travel to the island is scheduled to continue until 15 March next year. Decisions regarding access to the ecologically critical destination were reached during an interministerial meeting at the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on 12 October. Following the meeting, the ministry’s Environment-2 wing issued directives to relevant departments to implement the access plan. Under the new regulations, a maximum of 3,500 tourists will be permitted to visit the island each day, and each visitor is required to pay an environmental conservation fee of Tk 100. The Department of Environment has been instructed to collect these fees in accordance with the Environment Conservation Area Management Rules, 2016. Approved tourist vessels will continue to operate from the Nuniyachhara jetty. Additionally, the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA) and the Department of Shipping are prohibited from permitting vessel operations to the island without approval from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

parsed.headline: African experts discuss climate adaptation measurement at workshop in Ghana

pages.text: At the African Technical Workshop on the Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA) Indicators held in Accra, Ghana, participants discussed the necessity of measuring climate adaptation by its impact on human lives rather than financial expenditure. The three-day workshop, held from 22 to 24 October 2026 at the West African Genetic Medicine Centre, convened African climate negotiators, government officials, technical experts, and representatives from the United Nations University and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The central task of the event was to test if global adaptation indicators can reflect Ghana’s national priorities, identify what existing data systems can measure, and determine where data gaps exist. This exercise follows the adoption of 59 Belém Adaptation Indicators under the Global Goal on Adaptation process. Dr. Richard Munang, Director of the United Nations University Institute for Natural Resources in Africa (UNU-INRA), stated that adaptation should be judged by who is protected rather than what is spent. He argued that adaptation policies and investments must connect to tangible improvements in people's lives, noting that failing to count what is failing makes it impossible to fix.

parsed.headline: Jamuna Bank launches entrepreneurship training program in Panchagarh, Bangladesh

pages.text: Jamuna Bank PLC launched a 100-hour, month-long Entrepreneurship Development Training Program on October 19, 2026, at the RDRS Training Centre in Panchagarh, according to a press release reported by The Financial Express Bangladesh. The program is organized under the Skills for Industry Competitiveness and Innovation Program (SICIP), which is funded by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and implemented by the Finance Division of the Ministry of Finance, with supervision from the SME & Special Programs Department of Bangladesh Bank. The inaugural ceremony was attended by Mohammed Walid Hossain, Executive Program Director of SICIP and Additional Secretary of the Finance Division, Ministry of Finance, who served as the Chief Guest. Hossain described the initiative as a milestone for developing entrepreneurs and supporting economic growth.

The ceremony was chaired by Noor Mohammed, Deputy Managing Director and Chief Business Officer of Jamuna Bank PLC. Special guests included Myenul Hasan, Deputy Executive Program Director of SICIP and Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Finance; Mahmuda Akhter, Assistant Executive Program Director of SICIP and Deputy Secretary of the Ministry of Finance; and Md. Masum Billah, Program Director of SICIP and Additional Director of Bangladesh Bank. Other attendees included Md. Wasim, Joint Director of Bangladesh Bank and Deputy Project Director; Nasrul Hadi Mohammad Nusrat, SAVP and Head of SME Marketing at Jamuna Bank PLC; and Md. Rashed Mamun, AVP and Manager of Jamuna Bank's Panchagarh Branch.
